purpose: This medication is used to treat an underactive thyroid gland, a condition called hypothyroidism. When your thyroid doesn't make enough hormones on its own, this medicine replaces them. It helps your body's metabolism, energy levels, and many other functions get back to normal.
how_it_works: Your thyroid gland normally makes hormones that control how your body uses energy. This medication is made from the dried thyroid glands of pigs and contains two natural thyroid hormones, T3 and T4. Once you take it, your body absorbs these hormones and uses them just like the ones your thyroid would normally make.
common_side_effects: Most side effects happen if your dose is too high and include a fast or pounding heartbeat, feeling nervous or jittery, trouble sleeping, sweating more than usual, feeling too warm, weight loss, and headaches. If you notice any of these, let your doctor know right away.
warnings: Do not use this medicine to treat obesity or for weight loss — it can be dangerous at high doses. Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, diabetes, or adrenal gland problems before starting this medication. It can interact with other medicines like blood thinners, antacids, and calcium supplements, so always tell your pharmacist about everything you take. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very personal and depends on your lab results and how you feel. Most adults start with a low dose, often around 30 mg once a day in the morning on an empty stomach, and the doctor slowly adjusts it over time. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to make sure you are on the right dose.
